notes.title: Re-education room and new helper system!
notes.content:
Greetings to all the gifted blacksmiths!
 
We have prepared a brand-new update for everyone who loves the tale of Arthur and his friends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/cc2528e5409ac2f5f6f2490e052035c30155844c.png[/img]

A new cutscene will fill you in on what happened to Arthur between the first fair and the beginning of the main game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/55b0f3c4b62ee34f142598b665dae8d2aafe8454.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/5d37c7c3a737acbde3f76405f8ae79dabfe9bcec.png[/img]

Anvil Saga now features decorations and a lighting system for rooms. You can now purchase over 20 new items that will allow you to further customize each space to your liking.

The "re-education room" allows you to remove unnecessary perks and to reroll character traits. But be careful, because there is a downside: after removing a perk, the character loses some health and will temporarily receive the "dizziness" perk.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/6df9b0794d1f343076e2e97cabaf94b0fe90b2e5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/72fa9b52a29d0dfd535e3556f6b8fc9eb04caa26.png[/img]

We also added a "helper" system, which allows you to hire a variety of helpers with unique bonuses. After repairing the helper's cabin, you will have access to a hunter, a lumberjack, a treasurer, an old soldier, and a minstrel all for a reasonable fee.

Finally, there are new side quests for day 44. You'll find out how the stories of Gobin or Danna will end. 

We can't wait for you to play the new update! Share your impressions of the game here or in our official [url=https://discord.gg/M83fnAbgWT]Discord[/url]. 

Regards,
Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: What awaits you in the third chapter of the Anvil Saga and more
notes.content:
Greetings to all the gifted blacksmiths!

We're nearing the full release of Anvil Saga, and, in the meantime, we want to tell you about all of the features you can expect in the highly-anticipated update.

There will be new content, from the continuation of the story's finale to a wide range of changes in the previously released chapters. There will be two new quests waiting for you, which will further affect the story. In order to play through them, you'll need to start the game again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/91ac23361b03cbfc233dc59a5cc1fe7dcd476e47.png[/img]

During the third chapter of the game, Arthur will face harsh new challenges, such as a  terrible disease that has swept across the province. And the final battle will influence whether England, France, or the Bandits will prevail.

The length of the plague, the lives of several heroes, and the outcome of the final battle will directly depend on your decisions. Choose carefully – the fate of the province depends on you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/a28d685a65abcddd83b7ac38aebc57298235b503.png[/img]

In the Anvil Saga finale, Arthur and Jean-Jacques will face off in a blacksmith's duel within the imposing walls of the Baron's castle. You'll need to fulfill visitor's orders to decide the outcome of this epic tale.

We have created six different endings for Arthur and Jean-Jacques, and you will learn the fate of the Baron,the  faction heads, Finley, Olivia, Vlad, and even the Headman! Your actions will affect their fate, determining whether they will live happy lives or not. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/3bbdf7449117248fbf20770090abd66d5737e9a3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/ae2727d07d858d558257c95ac559d37503dfd8e4.png[/img]

This update will also contain the wood carving mechanic. Arthur will have to master not only the skills of a carpenter but also a carver.  Life in the Middle Ages was hard and you needed a lot of skills to survive.

The full release update for Anvil Saga will include:
[list]
[*] More than 10 hours of exciting gameplay;
[*] More than 30 complex customers with special needs and outlandish orders;
[*] Around 90 regular customers visiting the forge every day looking for a solution to their everyday problems;
[*] Story characters who can become either friend or foe of Arthur;
[*] 25 modifiers that affect gameplay and your business tactics;
[*] Plenty of quests and side-quests;
[*] Oddball apprentices with their own peculiarities, including funny and not so funny buffs and debuffs for them;
[*] 4 the stall levels and lots of decor for the forge of your dreams;
[*] A variety of end game options. 
[/list]
Thank you for supporting our small team throughout the development of Anvil Saga. Sharing your impressions, suggesting ideas, and helping us to find bugs has been an absolute joy. 

If Anvil Sags is not in your Steam library yet, it's time to add it there!

See you soon in a small, still French, province behind the anvil and furnace. 

Regards,
Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: The new Anvil Saga update is available now!
notes.content:
Greetings to all the gifted blacksmiths!

We are releasing a new update with a number of important changes and bug fixes for Anvil Saga.

First of all, Arthur can no longer obtain the "Pacifist" trait. This has been requested by the warlike players since the game was first released – if you're one of them, let us know in the comments below.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_2fb0c47fc3fe45a081e9fb27223a94a1~mv2.gif[/img]

The order feed's priority list has been changed. Now there can be only one order with a certain priority, instead of several. For example, only a single order with a priority of "1", "2", "3", etc. We also added the ability to drag and drop order cards. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/c8015ce1a84cc8f08fced9eac4a574305389e7d2.png[/img]

Improved the mechanics of equipping workers. Each blacksmith has a pool of three items and will automatically switch between them for the most efficient work completion on a particular machine. The equipment interface has also been redesigned specifically for this mechanic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/7af97ab1ad23db1c58ec89daed76d3435a238351.png[/img]

The workers' remuneration was overhauled to appear in a separate window, similar to the tax payment system. A worker's mood will decrease if you refuse to pay them.

[*] Added the ability for the player to accept story orders that require wood, even if the player does not have a workbench. 
[*] Increased the capacity of log racks. 
[*] Fixed prices for logs. 
[*] Fixed the conditions for building the bottom left room in the mine.
[*] Added new achievements!
[/list]

notes.title: Meet the Anvil Saga team!
notes.content:
Greetings to all the gifted blacksmiths!

New Year's Eve is upon us! While you're getting ready to celebrate with your family and friends, we decided to introduce you to the Anvil Saga team. In this post, we'll share what each one of us handles on the project, why we love Anvil Saga, and what inspires us to forge a game about being a blacksmith.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/28eb0e8dcca463b0d60f61bcccd9a768affdb547.png[/img]

[h3][b]Timur, the author and programmer at Anvil Saga.[/b][/h3]

I've always liked games and wanted to create one of my own. I started to get interested in gaming at the age of 13 – it all started with learning Game Maker. After about a year, I switched to Unity and a year after that, my first project, Life is Hard, was available on Steam.

I've been developing almost every day since then, and it's safe to say that it's my hobby and favorite thing to do – it's not a job. Also, I've always loved history, and Anvil Saga, as a game in a historical setting, is perfect for me.

I love watching other people play Anvil Saga. Seeing tens of thousands of people play your project is an indescribable feeling. Since I'm the only programmer on the team, there were – and still are – quite a few challenges. But I see the project getting better and better each month, and that inspires me to work more.

I wish all players more awesome games and more spare time to play them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/e3ea7f574458e5b024dcee7c62286b6bbe6b42ea.png[/img]

[h3][b]Evgeny, creative alias Pixel_Poem, pixel art artist and animator. [/b][/h3]

I've been working on Arthur's adventures for about two years now, and I'm responsible for all the visuals in the game. Before Anvil Saga, I spent several years working on Police Stories and created some very discreet projects for myself.

I love pixel art, classic 2D or 3D doesn't really appeal to me. The process of drawing and animation is like working with a mosaic, the most important thing is to arrange the squares in the right order, add a little chaos, and the output ends up being a cool picture or animation. To work with all this, I am inspired by my beloved wife Katerina.

Anvil Saga is my craziest project – in a good way. It's hard to find such fun, tons of references, and humor wrapped up in the harsh everyday life of a young blacksmith. It's because of this craziness that I am grateful for the game and our team. A special thanks to our producer, Daniil, because without him, this fun would be out of control.

And to you, dear players, I want to wish you a happy New Year. And most importantly – good pixel games. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/5eb68073f2bb8fd1d7611cef017a52d58df55ed6.png[/img]

[h3][b]Peter, the narrative designer of Anvil Saga.[/b][/h3]

Anvil Saga was my first gameplay project, for which I am very grateful! I enjoy creating and designing characters and events, and really hope they bring you enjoyable emotions. Blacksmith Arthur and his friends (as well as enemies) are already like family, and I'm always excited to create new quests. 

My work is inspired by cool games, of which there are more every year. I believe the gaming industry has an incredible future, and I'm excited to be a small part of it. 

To all the players of Anvil Saga, I wish you a great New Year! May the customers pay the blacksmith generously in 2023, may there always be enough materials, and may the French finally make peace with the English! Happy holidays to all!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/1d65040ed67d817009335e18ef573cd8cd4730e1.png[/img]

[h3][b]Daniil, producer on the HeroCraft PC side and game designer.[/b][/h3]

I started my journey in game development as a marketing manager, but I quickly realized that I was more interested in the development process itself, so I first moved into project management, and then into production.

What I love most about my work is to see how ideas are implemented into real content and mechanics, and how they form a complete game. I don't like routines. What inspires me to work is the path from the beginning to the final result. I love comparing the early versions to the final. I can't help but be motivated by the way projects change from prototype to final game.

Anvil Saga is like my adopted child. The lovely visual style, witty dialogues, and gameplay that allows you to to vibe and relax – at the same time, it requires concentration and decision-making. When I worked on Anvil Saga, I wanted to make the game to please me as a player first, not as a producer. I hope that it pleases you as well.

I wish our players that their forges grow and develop, and their provinces experience not a hundred years of war, but rather a thousand years of prosperity.

Our team is small but very friendly and hardworking. We love Anvil Saga and strive to make the game as original and exciting as possible, so that you will love it even more. 

Stay in touch with us here and on [url=https://discord.gg/XVMJFp4nsP]Discord[/url]. We love the Anvil Saga community and always read your thoughts and suggestions about the game.  

Regards,
Anvil Saga Team

Modifiers will not only change the visuals in Anvil Saga, but also will force you to be clever and creative in solving complex business problems.

[*] Beaujolais Day;

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_66d0e48bbdea4dd69408f61ad2024dff~mv2.gif [/img]

notes.title: New in-game interface! Can you spot the difference?

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_dc0d0cb6eb8a438cbf455166cb12441a~mv2.gif[/img]

The order feed contains all of the requests that you have accepted, whether they're regular, bulk, complex, or quest-related. To keep things organized, you can easily change the priority of every order, each of which will also have a count-down timer.

[list]

[*] Time remaining to complete the order.
[*] An image of the item.
[/list]
[b]The bulk orders[/b] are separated by item and include a counter for the number of items already completed.

For [b]Complex orders[/b] the cards are divided by order parts. Once you have created all the required parts, a new order for assembling the item will appear. Once the assembly is complete, the order is considered completed too.

And in addition to the interface design, we continue to populate the world of Anvil Saga with new characters. Here's another potential assistant to Arthur.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/063e69151935fc5b37fad97a249f6f8038f393c3.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Forging ahead in a time of war
notes.content:
Greetings! 

We've previously talked about how the different seasons can greatly affect the gameplay of Anvil Saga, but what about the war? After all, the game is set during the Hundred Years' War so surely there are skirmishes taking place?

[url=https://ibb.co/6wmjt71][img]https://i.ibb.co/fF2jNzn/f1192deea50576a4569579fb53a1db64.gif[/img][/url] 

Military tents and garrisons litter the countryside, while campfires roar as soldiers sing songs to boost morale. Of course, soldiers and knights will be your main customers during times of conflict.

notes.title: Winter snows and summer heat: which is the best?
notes.content:
Greetings! 

The flow of time is a large part of the gameplay in Anvil Saga. In our previous demo, players experienced the day and night cycle that we implemented. Today, we are proud to announce that the seasons will also change in Anvil Saga!

The new mechanic drastically affects resource balance and NPC activities. Let’s take a quick look.

[url=https://ibb.co/4g1FxmZ][img]https://i.ibb.co/0Vsn3Dj/f0a16fced48fd8f234ec7dec1a6020e4.gif[/img][/url]

During spring, the peasants are busy sowing fields for new harvests. However, there isn't much food left over from the previous year's supplies. This will not only lead to an influx of peasants, but also much higher food prices. 

In summer, Arthur will enjoy the green trees and warm, sunny days – working in the forge is a pleasure. However, summer days can also be too hot and dry, resulting in forest fires that directly contribute to an increase in the cost of wood. Hunters will then avoid the province, and you'll also see a reduction of peasants visiting your forge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/f1b81dfd778b0acd9a3609faa0f824874fb92f64.png[/img]

Autumn is the time when new crops are harvested. This may sometimes create an overabundance of vegetables. Peasants will offer to pay you with their bounties, but it's up to you whether to accept them instead of gold. 

Winter might look serene and beautiful, but it brings with it many dangers. You could find yourself in the middle of a storm or severe frost span that leaves devastating effects. What are they? Well, you'll have to find out for yourself :)

Furthermore, snow is a harbinger of Christmas, which is also celebrated in the medieval French provinces.

Add Anvil Saga to your Steam Wishlist and keep checking back for all of the latest development news. Something exciting will be unveiled very soon!

[i]Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team[/i]

When a faction's reputation reaches a certain amount, you will receive a buff or debuff from that faction. For example, if your relationship with France was soured, the French will spread rumors about your forge, which will lead to a decrease in prestige every day. If you sabotage relations with the Holy Church, spiteful clerics will ring the bells in the morning to prevent your workers from resting. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/d34b77c0177659ca3e87c630991b45b95a7c103b.png[/img]

However, if your reputation is high enough, you will gain certain preferential treatment. The English may declare a tax holiday in the region and collect taxes less often. If you are friendly with the bandits, they may station a bouncer outside your forge to extort extra cash from customers. 

Each faction can influence the game and make Arthur's life a little bit easier or more difficult. It's up to you to decide which one to support!

notes.title: Reputation in the time of war
notes.content:
Greetings! 

Our team is happy to report that faction related mechanics have been fine-tuned, as well as the associated buffs and debuffs, which we'll cover in the next update. 

As you know, there are five factions in Anvil Saga: England, France, the Holy Church, the Witches and the Bandits. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/280654a3c0686662a4fd8b7d2a8b1d34ba2e1c47.png[/img]

All orders now carry unique designations associated with each faction. This makes choosing which orders you want to fulfil first that much easier. Once an order is completed, a colored number will appear above the customer's head, representing the change in reputation for that faction. 

England, France and Bandits accrue reputation from five types of customers: knights, soldiers, peasants, merchants and hunters. Knights, soldiers and hunters will only come if the province is under the control of their faction. Hunters may also drop in during archery competitions. Though, peasants and merchants of all factions will visit at any time. 

Keep in mind that merchants and hunters do not like competition. For example, if you fulfill an order for a French merchant or hunter, all English merchants and hunters will immediately leave the queue. Politics sure are tricky! 

To increase reputation with the Holy Church or the Witches, you will have to complete orders from priests and witches respectively. 

Bandits will not be affected by this decision, but they don't like to be turned down. If you choose to not fulfill an order from a customer belonging to the Bandit faction, your reputation with the faction will be lowered. 

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Blacksmith's work-life balance
notes.content:
Greetings! 

The art of blacksmithing requires physical strength, focus and attention – becoming a true craftsman is no easy task! But Anvil Saga isn't just about you. After all, you have a shop to run and employees to look after. In fact, we’ve been busy fine-tuning all of the associated mechanics in the game to make sure that running a blacksmith shop during the Middle Ages is as interesting as possible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/824b664211563e2c032e3401ff880754eb487aa6.png[/img]

For example, the health of Arthur and his apprentices depends primarily on satisfaction and energy levels. Working from dawn until dusk without resting will lead to a loss in efficiency. Exhausted workers are more likely to make mistakes and take longer to complete orders.

Sick workers are more prone to injuries, which could lead to your staff seriously hurting themselves or even dying! As soon as you notice that a worker isn't feeling well, let them rest or have something to eat. Just keep in mind that a stale meal won't do them any good, either. 

If a worker's health becomes critical, they might become a burden to you – even if they're recovering at home, you'll still have to pay their wages. Only a doctor, one that also costs money, can heal the sick or gravely injured.

Do you have what it takes to maintain a healthy work-life balance and to stop the forge from running into labor issues? Time will tell ;)


Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga team

notes.title: Everyone to the fair!
notes.content:
Greetings! 

Fairs were one of the most important social events in the Middle Ages. Merchants and craftsmen from far and wide would travel to these events. They would prepare for the fair in advance, selecting their best wares and products to garner as much gold as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/d3fe8d2bd92aba9bb5706ee02336bbf927e955bb.png[/img]

The Anvil Saga Fair is all about honoring the leading faction in the war, trading, dancing, as well as a battle between rival blacksmiths. Arthur will get the chance to show off his skills and face off against Jean-Jacques Jr. in a smithing duel. The winner will receive the title of Best Master, and will be one step closer to becoming the Baron's Court Blacksmith.

This is why Arthur needs to prepare for the fair. The more you invest in the event, the more ore and bars you can take with you. You can also bring along more manpower, so think about inviting your most talented worker. Together, you can complete more orders and make as much coin as possible. And don't forget about the importance of first impressions. A fancy tent will bring in more customers than a shabby one. 

Despite all of Arthur's careful preparation, it won't be easy to beat Jean-Jacques Jr. The war between France and England is not only affecting the powerful, but also ordinary artisans. At the fair, you'll have to assess each customer's country of origin and decide whether to take the order. It's unlikely that the dominant faction will be happy to see you forging swords and horseshoes for their enemies.

Pack up your best tools and head to the fair! Towards fame, fortune and love. 

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga team

notes.title: Become the Court Blacksmith
notes.content:
Greetings! 

Besides winning the heart of his love and reviving his father's business, protagonist Arthur is also after the position of Court Blacksmith.

The Baron is the main man of the land, sly as a fox and cruel as a wolf. He masterfully plays both the English and French forces, firmly retaining his power in these troubled times. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/f4e95c094efd2d5f130c069c919c86020eed9209.png[/img]

Earning the respect of such a powerful man is no easy task. The Baron will regularly visit your smithy with special orders. His attitude towards you will depend on how diligently you fulfill his requests. If the job is done well, he will not only help you gain position in society, but you will have his support in the most unexpected situations. 

However, your rival, the sly Jean-Jacques Jr., also fights for the Baron's patronage and the position of Court Blacksmith. You'll have to work hard to beat this French dealer.

Fire up the forge! Don't leave Jean-Jacques Jr. any chance of winning.

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Antonio's specialty store
notes.content:
Greetings!

While playing Anvil Saga, you may need to work on complex orders that involve using less common resources such as gems and various types of ore. We'd like to introduce you to Antonio, the procurer of rare materials.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/efb0b68f77ce09e5602527e7bd21ec7fc0dade4f.png[/img]

Antonio is a merchant who specialises in a variety of goods. You will gain access to his shop after completing one of the main quests. For a bit of gold, he will supply you with the necessary materials for fulfilling complex or story-driven orders throughout the game.

As soon as you need an item, it will appear in Antonio's shop. These items are unique and only one of each exists in Anvil Saga, so you won't be able to purchase them in advance or at a lower price. Be prepared! It's worth having a small cash reserve just in case. 

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Forge your fame
notes.content:
Greetings!

In Anvil Saga, you can't establish a prestigious blacksmith business without name recognition to draw in new, wealthy customers. The "fame" indicator is an important one to keep an eye on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/e998e31eac434dc7af4ab82b18be3845f95feb45.png[/img]

The only way to increase the fame of your forge is to fulfil orders. Word of mouth is a powerful advertising tool. Creating excellent work with a quick turnaround time will attract more and more wealthy customers.

With every new level of "fame", you can expand the business with new rooms, decorations, tools and staff. Basically, the more people know about your blacksmithing prowess, the more money will come your way.

Make sure to keep the storefront appealing by using decorations and expensive furniture. After all, it doesn't hurt to show off your wealth ;)

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Meet the carpenter!
notes.content:
Greetings!

Building your blacksmithing business isn't just about forging weapons; you'll need to branch out into other areas, like woodworking. During the Middle Ages, wooden implements were always in demand, and trees for timber were in abundance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/356f3836267cefc403a2e06731081170754e6eab.jpg[/img]

To sell wooden items, you're going to need a carpenter. You can either hire an experienced carpenter for your forge or train an apprentice from scratch. It's a very specific vocation that requires skill and dedication to master. 

Orders for wooden items are carried out separately from those that need to be forged. Before your carpenter can start on an order, you will need to purchase logs and then have them carved into usable lumber boards. 

Sometimes, peasants will barter boards for orders, much like they do with food during harvests. It's a reasonable way to accumulate raw materials instead of paying for them.

Remember to keep stock of as many resources as possible, train your employees to bring out their potential and increase your forge's fame to grow your business!


Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Workers and their quirks
notes.content:
Greetings!

Arthur and his employees are more than just NPCs in a game that blindly fulfill tasks. In fact, each one of them has special traits that make them unique in Anvil Saga. Over time, they will acquire new traits to add to their collection of foibles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/01a60efc8fb75a1b8b7d551489cad756c32cee6e.jpg[/img]

Special traits will positively and negatively alter the way you run your forge. For example, anyone with the "pacifist" trait will refuse to fulfil orders associated with war. These workers are better used to create consumables or extract resources. The "underground man" is happy to just live on mushrooms he finds in the mine. Send him to extract ore and don't worry about his hunger needs.

And then there are "Night Owl" or "Early bird" buffs that enable a character to perform their tasks better during certain times of the day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/fb706ea1d9bece56c93104c1dce4674709bd8c09.png[/img]

In Anvil Saga, employees can also have temporary boosts and weaknesses. If a nest of spiders falls onto the ore miner's head, they won't go back underground for a long time (would you?). If a worker spends too much time in the sun, they'll develop heatstroke and will get tired faster.

No one is immune from buffs and debuffs. You will have to give your employees time to recover before they are able to work at full capacity again. However, if they have a surge of energy, be sure to allocate complex tasks to them and reap the rewards.

As in life, delegation is key to running a successful business!


Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Matters of the Heart
notes.content:
Greetings!

Every story set in Medieval times needs a fair maiden, and Anvil Saga has one! Meet Olivia, the most beautiful woman in the French province; Arthur has been enamored with her since they were young.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/46fd27adc230070e75d097b231906d36558ba1e3.png[/img]

Olivia's father, Finley, is a successful and respected smith. While he is fond of Arthur, he wants his daughter to marry into wealth, which is why she is betrothed to Jean-Jacues Jr. The problem is that Finley does not know that his soon-to-be son-in-law is just a pretender, unskilled with an anvil and hot iron.

Arthur only has a couple of years to prove that he is worthy of Olivia's hand in marriage and that he can support her. Medieval problems, right?

Arthur's relationship with Olivia and Finley will develop throughout Anvil Saga. By completing orders with a touch of finesse – by adding in extra resources and care during production – you can outdo Jean-Jacques Jr. and prove that you have the chops to run a successful business.

However, unlike her father, Olivia is not interested in trade. Her heart aches for all the victims of the war. You will receive unique orders from her that will help the ones hurt and burdened. Speedily completing these orders will see Olivia’s feelings grow towards Arthur.

You need to earn the favor of Finley and Olivia –  please do not leave Arthur alone in his prime. He does not need fire, but love to keep him warm and happy.

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Rivals in Business — and in Love
notes.content:
Greetings!

Every hero needs an antagonist, someone who stands in their way, is a constant obstacle, and always one move ahead. Anvil Saga has one of those! Meet Jean-Jacques Junior, the villain of our story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/c165e541fad3cabcd20bd96f14103241a661238f.png[/img]

Jean-Jacques Senior was one of the wealthiest smiths in the French region. Arthur's father was a blacksmith who arrived from England and settled in a neighboring village. Jean-Jacques Sr. was not happy about the arrival of a foreign competitor. Even though the two held mutual respect for each other and the craft, their rivalry continued beyond their deaths and passed on to their sons.

Jean-Jacques Junior makes up for his middling smithcraft with excellent entrepreneurship. A rich inheritance and his skills in organizing a workforce led his smithy to prosperity and made him the main pretender not only to the title of the Baron’s court smith, but also to the heart and hand of the province’s greatest beauty, our hero’s beloved.

It is up to you to make sure Arthur's blacksmithing business is successful, to overtake his rival and to  find love. 


Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Special orders from special customers
notes.content:
Greetings!

Blacksmithing in the Middle Ages wasn't all that exciting – make a few nails, some horseshoes, and that was it. In Anvil Saga, we are spicing things up via the orders you will get to work on. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/41482942ad86d389d268c6f44599055df9bd02f4.jpg[/img]

From time to time, unique customers will visit your forge and commission you to create items that are quite extraordinary. These are not regular commodities that Arthur encounters every day, and he will have to work extra hard to forge each one.

The items can require a variety of skills to create. It's not enough to forge a blade and make a hilt, the sword may need to be inlaid with a faceted gem. It will require a lot of work, but will be a sight to behold once the weapon is ready.

You will receive orders of various complexity and price, and a limited time in which to complete them. Of course, no one will wait an eternity for their unique item. 

If you succeed and the customer is happy, you will receive a handsome income and the prestige of your forge will increase. A higher prestige means even more famous (or infamous) customers will visit your store, each with their own interesting history and a request.

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Something new every day
notes.content:
Greetings!

Running a business is never easy, especially during times of war. Despite the profitability of blacksmithing, your income and success will depend not only on your forging skills, but also your ability to adapt to any circumstance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/cd4862c961d789d0b89bb0965b781fc0d94aef9c.png[/img]

Each new day may be different from the previous one thanks to the event system. Life in the village goes on as usual, seasons change, armies raise and lower new flags, and Arthur continues to fan fires and forge yet another order. Here are just some of the events that may occur throughout your gameplay session:

[list]
[*] Holidays. As part of the preparation for the festivities, tents are set up, fences are fixed and decorations installed. While this sounds fun, it also means that wood has rapidly increased in price. If you really need to restock your supplies, prepare to fork out. Fortunately (or unfortunately, depending on the relationships you’ve established), if the holiday event is associated with any of the game’s factions, their representatives will come to your shop more often. 

[*] Sowing and harvesting. Peasants everywhere! They come in pairs and will usually pay for their order with vegetables, but they may be willing to part with coin for the right tools. 

[*] Floods, forest fires, rainstorms - each one affects your life and your business in a different way. If the roads are washed out, for example, most of the customers simply will not be able to reach you. 
[/list]

All this, along with local clashes, celebrations, large construction projects and more, will make Arthur's life incredibly diverse and...interesting. Each event has a variety of consequences, both positive and negative. The ability to adapt and take advantage of any situation is what distinguishes a real businessman. Good luck in this difficult endeavor!

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: A few special customers
notes.content:
Greetings!

War is a time when not only armies thrive, but also skillful mercenaries. Anyone that can hold a sword may set out on a quest to prove themselves, to fight for glory. 

But not all of your customers will be regular swordsmen. In fact, a few of them are quite unique individuals. And you might already know some of them :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/0aaf35de7df9ebbba69aba61f70bd1301c7caae6.png[/img]

Here are a few examples of the items you will need to craft:
[list]
 [*]An axe combined with a saw.
 [*]A hidden wrist blade.
 [*]A sterling silver sword.
 [*]A metal-framed hiking backpack.
 [*]A keurig used to make alcoholic beverages.
[/list]
The last item might not seem that important to a mercenary, but believe us, it’s a must when it comes to saving lives. You can probably guess who all of these items belong to ;)

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: The Hundred Years War and Young Arthur
notes.content:
Greetings!

Anvil Saga takes place during the Hundred Years War, a series of prolonged conflicts between France and England that went on from 1337 to 1453, interspersed with short periods of peace. It was a difficult time for both countries and for the several generations of common people who lived there. But how does smithing come into all this?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/3959eb98982d3497d974b71bfdae64229fa92131.jpg[/img]

Smiths – with the exception of Wat Tyler, who led a massive peasant rebellion – fully dedicated themselves to supporting the armies of their countries. They carried out military orders in their own smitheries and marched together with the troops so they would be able to offer quick fixes on the spot.

A myriad of different tasks fell on their shoulders: from farriery and maintenance to crafting new arms and equipment. An army without an adequate blacksmith to support it was doomed to fatal losses. After a number of encounters, soldiers could become so poorly equipped that their effectiveness would plummet to the level of the peasant militia, and no amount of training could recoup that.

Despite the destructive nature of the conflicts, war was quite a lucrative industry and prosperous time for every master of the craft whose services were required by the state. During these years, blacksmith craftsmanship and finesse grew immensely, which led to the emergence of new types of weapons and armor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/c69a56e036cd9a22fcb446ec6175f71977b83781.jpg[/img]

In Anvil Saga, you manage Arthur’s smithy, which is located in a frontier village. The baron in charge of the land that your settlement is located in is a turncoat – as were many other landlords of that time. No one knows how the war will go, and both England and France could claim ownership over your little commune. Your decisions will be crucial in deciding which way the story will go from here.

If you choose to support one of the factions, carry out their orders and supply them with arms, you would help them to occupy the town. Would this affect the outcome of the war? Hardly. But in this town, you could change a lot of lives. Use your power wisely.

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: Worker features
notes.content:
Greetings!

It’s impossible to run a business without hiring employees. This is what lies in store for you, too. War is devastating, armies need supplies, ordinary citizens need essentials, and you need helpers. Therefore, today we will look at getting help for your business.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/fdde8d30b72d10a4d84f84f4d504e996346c8fb4.png[/img]

Soon after having opened a forge, you’ll understand that there are few professions out there in such high demand as blacksmithing. The line of customers goes on and on, and you’re completely exhausted. In order to effectively complete your orders, you’re going to need another pair of hands. Luckily, there are several apprentices, who want to work for you. Pick one, anyone will do! Or not?

Every worker has features that will affect your business. A pacifist blacksmith will never accept orders from soldiers, as he is bound by his personal code. You might say there's no place for such stubbornness in this business. We say cheap labor is for the mines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/b4a1da5b5e6a1a91192402a559bc98d791da8684.png[/img]

Among the applicants you'll see both religious folk and ex-criminals who can extort some extra cash from simple peasants. They can be talented and skilled, or total screw-ups who’ll need to be trained from scratch. More often than not these features will be hidden, but you can pay your trusted sources a little something for additional info.

Regardless of whom you choose, these guys will have your back when it all goes down. Eventually, they'll become essential workers through developing their skills and will be able to learn new specialties such as woodcarving or jewelry.

That's all for today. Be on the lookout for the messenger next week!

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: How your decisions affect the game world
notes.content:
Greetings!

As you've probably figured out, things aren't always that simple in the world of Anvil Saga. Especially when you're just a blacksmith that has to balance the interests of five rival factions. Today, you'll learn how a little man can change the life of a whole village.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/0049050ade52497e52166a7a60f10bdb877b0569.png[/img]

Apart from being able to pick a certain faction and attempt to win their favor for a reward (which we talked about last time), you can also react to various events that pop up regularly.

One day, you may receive an order for a large amount of tools that are needed to build a new levee. Your goal is to complete the order before the river swells. If you decline the order or don’t finish it on time, the village will be flooded. Under these circumstances, the villagers are less likely to come to you with new orders.

But the choice presented by this event isn’t that simple ;) Successful construction of a levee will eventually drain the nearby forest, which, in turn, will lead to forest fires during the hot summer. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/7b3e2f170819ac701cff3095fafa1da4fa2401fd.png[/img]

You can always ignore an event, but your inaction has consequences. A merchant’s broken cart, a bandit attack, the arrival of an army – almost any situation, no matter how dire, can be used to your advantage. But make the wrong move, and you’ll upset the delicate balance, causing unrest, losing a worker or even damaging the local economy.

That's all for today. Be on the lookout for the messenger next week!

Respectfully,
The Anvil Saga Team

notes.title: A conflict of interests and swords
notes.content:
Greetings!

Messengers, bearing the latest news on Anvil Saga, have been sent out. To start things off, today, we're talking about Factions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/ca3b35e0832cd39a96b166f5e3294d8eb09904c7.jpg[/img]

In Anvil Saga, there are two major forces for you to balance between: England and France. The game is set during the Hundred Years’ War, when the two sides were competing for territory. Ordinary citizens had no choice but to adapt to the conflict in order to survive.

As the player, you take on the role of a blacksmith – a profitable business during wartime! Still, don’t expect money to just flow like a river; favoring one side of the war will inevitably upset the other.

To give you a specific example, one of the unfortunate aspects of war is an event called the "Influx of Refugees". An abundance of destitute individuals can be difficult for any settlement, let alone a small village where you’ve set up shop. You can appeal to either England or France to assist you with the new people, but each option will come with its own consequences.

One side will agree to recruit the majority of the vagrant men as soldiers, which will increase the number of military contracts available to you. As for the other side, well… you'll just have to play the game to find out ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40267025/35705bd7092d288c687a51a0ee24dc74c3fe2f80.jpg[/img]

Apart from the two warring nations, there are also three smaller factions sharing the same territory: Bandits, Clerics, and Witches. Each group wields a bit of power and has its own interests that may clash with the others'. For example, Bandits don't like authority, while Witches and Clerics both struggle to exert influence over the minds and souls of the local populace.

That being said, your overall strategy is to walk a fine line between the various factions, while giving preference to none. Or you can risk it all by allying with at least one of them to gain unique perks.

Do you want three extra workers? Ally with the English. How about casting lightning bolts on tax collectors? The Witches are your friends. If you're short on coin and want to extort an extra 10%, you can't go wrong with the Bandits.

That's all for today. Look out for another messenger next week!

Respectfully,
Anvil Saga Team
